thread:
security-bot: [alert] object-store:metadata-missing - manifest objects without SSE detected in redwood-db-snapshots/manifests/2026-08-04/ (severity: high)
maria: I pulled a manifest file and HEAD shows no x-amz-server-side-encryption. Manifest references ~900 snapshot keys. This means the list itself was uploaded unencrypted.
aj: running CloudTrail for PutObject to manifests/2026-08-04/ 01:00-03:00Z. Also checking caller principal.
luca: note: we rolled an uploader RBAC cleanup last week that removed a legacy policy binding. PR #6212. Could be related if metadata injection relied on that role.
raj-iam: I see a prune run at 02:10Z that removed grants scoped to older uploader principals. Will share exact change set.
maria: we need to treat this as P1 until we confirm whether snapshots themselves were encrypted or only the manifest. If manifest is cleartext, tenant mapping is exposed.
sam-oncall: immediate mitigation: block new manifest writes to that prefix. I can add a bucket policy requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption==aws:kms for manifests/* now.
aj: CloudTrail results: PutObject by arn:aws:sts::0123456789:assumed-role/svc-uploader at 02:21Z. No kms:GrantTokens in the call. Looks like uploader stopped attaching SSE metadata for manifests specifically.
luca: uploader code had a special-case that treats small manifest uploads differently (single PutObject path). Recent refactor moved SSE injection behind a wrapper that may not run for manifests.
raj-iam: also note we tested reducing ephemeral KMS grant TTL to 60s last month. If the grant expired before PutObject finished, the client might skip attaching tokens.
erin: from compliance perspective even manifest exposure needs timeline and tenant notification decisions. Please produce manifest key list and owner tenants quickly.
maria: remediation plan:
- block manifest writes (sam-oncall)
- fetch latest manifest and re-upload with --sse aws:kms with our CMK (aj)
- verify referenced snapshots' SSE headers and if any snapshot lacks SSE, schedule re-encrypt copy ops (luca + aj)
- run an Athena audit for PutObject where x-amz-server-side-encryption is null across snapshot and manifest prefixes (maria)
- produce compliance timeline and affected tenants (erin)

sam-oncall: applied deny policy to manifests/2026-08-04/* at 03:05Z. Monitoring failures.
aj: re-uploaded a copy of the manifest to a quarantine prefix with --sse aws:kms and attached to the incident. Will run checksum compare.
luca: writing a quick job to scan manifest entries and sample HEAD each referenced key to assert SSE header present; will surface any that need re-encrypt.
raj-iam: I'll revert the RBAC prune for the specific legacy binding until we finish investigation, and I'll review the grant TTL experiment - might need to restore previous TTL.
erin: got it - I'll prepare the customer notification checklist and escalate legal if tenants with stricter encryption clauses are affected.
maria: follow-ups after containment:
- add an automated alarm (Athena/CloudTrail) for PutObject without x-amz-server-side-encryption to snapshot/manifests prefixes
- add guard to RBAC-prune job to skip deleting bindings referenced by recent backup metadata
- require uploader CI test asserting SSE header for manifest uploads
- roll back KMS grant TTL experiment until uploader flow validated

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-722 created and assigned P1 responders: @maria @aj @luca @sam-oncall @erin @raj-iam
maria: thanks everyone. keep updates here and attach CSV of affected tenants to the incident doc when ready.
aj: uploading manifest key list + preliminary owner map to the incident page now.
